_comment: C4 regression gate. Consumed by `cmd/piano-distance --thresholds` and by `just gate-c4`.
A number under `max` is ENFORCED: the run fails (exit 2) when the measured metric
exceeds it. A `null` means NOT YET CALIBRATED - the metric is listed so its existence
is visible, but it is deliberately not enforced. Calibrating one later is a one-line
diff (replace the null with a number), not a new file. Any key here that is not a
float64 field of analysis.Metrics is an ERROR, so typos cannot silently disable a gate.
Thresholds are the value measured on the date in `recorded` plus 7.7-8.0% headroom,
rounded up to the precision used here. They are a regression fence, not a quality
target: tighten them whenever a fit genuinely improves.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-21 by the DWG treble-collapse fix. Two thresholds were LOOSENED,
which normally must not happen; the reasoning is in `recorded.note` and is not a
convenience. Two others were tightened in the same pass.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by the noteResonator unity-peak normalisation. ONE threshold was
LOOSENED - spectral_rmse_db 57.5 -> 67.0 - against an explicit written promise that the
real fix was a C4 re-fit against the corrected renderer.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-22 by that re-fit, which paid the promise off. ALL FIVE enforced
thresholds were TIGHTENED, spectral_rmse_db by the largest margin: 67.0 -> 61.0, whose
MEASURED value (56.572) is below the 57.5 that stood before the resonator
normalisation. Nothing here has been loosened since. Do not loosen anything again
without an equally explicit reason.
SPECTRAL CAVEAT: spectral_rmse_db is gated as a RAW dB value, which is a real regression
signal. The NORMALISED spectral component is a different matter - at 56.6 dB against
analysis.NormSpectral = 30.0 it is saturated, clamp01 pins it at 1.0, and it therefore
contributes a constant to `score` with no gradient for the optimizer. Every preset in
the repo saturates it (measured population range 47.8-68.6 dB on 2026-08-21).
This gate scores legacy-v1, which keeps the frozen norms and therefore keeps saturating;
that is the price of every recorded number staying comparable. The fix landed for the
profiles that steer the optimizer instead: analysis.CalibratedNorms raises Spectral to
80.0 (plus Decay, PartialLevel, PartialFreq, AttackRise and AttackCentroid) and is used
by balanced-v2, attack-v1, decay-v1 and inharmonicity-v1. legacy-v1 is untouched, so no
threshold and no recorded score moved because of it.
That saturation is also why the re-fit below was selected on balanced-v2 rather than on
legacy-v1: a search steered by legacy-v1 alone buys the four gated metrics with the six
un-gated ones, which is gate-gaming rather than a better model. See `recorded.note`.

note: C4 RE-FIT against the corrected renderer, 2026-08-22. This is the follow-up that the
previous re-baseline named as the honest remedy for the widened spectral fence, and it
is now paid off: `assets/presets/fitted-c4-mayfly.json` was re-fitted and all five
enforced thresholds were tightened in the same pass.
What moved, against the same preset path measured before the re-fit:
score               0.5249 -> 0.5182   threshold TIGHTENED 0.57  -> 0.559
time_rmse           0.10189 -> 0.10113 threshold TIGHTENED 0.112 -> 0.109
envelope_rmse_db   10.156  ->  9.593   threshold TIGHTENED 11.75 -> 10.34
spectral_rmse_db   62.287  -> 56.572   threshold TIGHTENED 67.0  -> 61.0
decay_diff_db_per_s 4.800  ->  4.503   threshold TIGHTENED 5.9   -> 4.85
The measured spectral_rmse_db (56.572) is back under the 57.5 that stood before the
resonator normalisation, so the spectrum is no longer tuned around the 1/f0
sympathetic-path defect. The CAP is 61.0 rather than something under 57.5 because the
7.7% headroom convention applies on top of the measurement; do not read the cap as a
claim that the fence is tighter than it was in 2026-08-21.
WHERE THE SPECTRAL GAIN CAME FROM. The dominant term was the wet level of the legacy single-IR (room) stage, not
anything in the string model. The preset carried ir_wet_mix 1.1888 with ir_gain 1.7203,
an effective wet factor of 2.045; a deterministic 2076-sample sweep of the three IR mix
knobs (`--sweep --optimize mix`, 9-point one-at-a-time scan plus 2048 Halton points,
report `out/sweep/mix-mayfly.json`) found 887 samples that improve ALL FOUR gated raw
metrics at once, so the region is large rather than a lucky sample. The re-fit sits at
ir_wet_mix 0.2328 / ir_gain 1.0912 / ir_dry_mix 0.2107, an effective wet factor of
0.254. Three further knobs came from pass sweeps around that point: high_freq_damping
0 -> 0.05 and unison_crossfeed 0.00236 -> 0.0025 (sustain box), and
per_note.60.strike_position 0.2945 -> 0.45 (inharmonicity box).
WHY THE SEARCH WAS SELECTED ON balanced-v2. legacy-v1 saturates its spectral component
and puts no weight at all on partial level, partial frequency, tristimulus, attack or
the segmented decay, so a search steered by it will happily pay those six to buy the
four it does see. That was measured, not assumed: a chain of deterministic pass sweeps
reached legacy-v1 0.4654 with spectral 48.1 and decay diff 1.54 - better on every gated
metric than the preset shipped here - while pushing partial_level_rmse_db from 10.88 to
24.20 and attack_centroid_rmse_oct from 0.544 to 2.445. That is gate-gaming, so it was
rejected. The shipped point is the balanced-v2 optimum of the same search: 0.47391 ->
0.42687, with no direction sampled around it improving balanced-v2 by more than 0.0002.
partial_level_rmse_db      10.883 -> 11.118  marginally worse
partial_freq_rmse_cents    36.609 -> 36.619  unchanged
tristimulus_distance        0.283 ->  0.231  improved
attack_rise_diff_ms        24.489 -> 24.395  unchanged
attack_centroid_rmse_oct    0.544 ->  0.947  WORSE
decay_segment_rmse_db_per_s 15.031 -> 14.345 improved
attack_centroid_rmse_oct    0.544 ->  0.947  WORSE
decay_segment_rmse_db_per_s 15.031 -> 11.075 improved
onset, so the candidate's attack centroid moves from 851 Hz to 1132 Hz against the
spectral gain: cutting the wet room IR removes most of the body colouration from the
onset, so the candidate's attack centroid moves from 851 Hz to 1131 Hz against the
reference's 586 Hz. It is not enforced here and was not enforced before; it is recorded
so the trade is visible rather than buried.
MEASUREMENT TRAP found while doing this and worth knowing. piano-fit's
`--match-output-gain` (default true) solves output_gain analytically after the search,
on the documented grounds that analysis.Compare RMS-normalises both signals so
differently. Measured on one fitted preset: output_gain 7.096 scores 0.5208 and
output_gain 1.357 scores 0.5061, same knobs otherwise. Normalising to the tracked
preset's output_gain is the right way to COMPARE candidates, and that is what was done
here. SHIPPING that normalised gain is not: cutting the IR mix cut the absolute level
with it, and at output_gain 1.357 the re-fitted preset rendered 7.2x quieter in RMS
(-25.6 -> -42.7 dBFS, peak -3.4 -> -21.5 dBFS) than the preset it replaces. The
RMS-normalising gate cannot see that. output_gain is therefore re-matched to 7.096,
which puts the render at 0.048274 RMS against the reference's 0.048364 (0.2%) with
peak 0.416, and EVERY number above is measured at that gain. The earlier column
measured at 1.357 (score 0.5040, spectral 51.554) is an artifact of the quiet render
and must not be quoted.
output_gain 1.357 scores 0.5061, same knobs otherwise. Every fitted preset in this
round was therefore re-measured at the tracked preset's output_gain.
Re-voicing this preset's resonance_gain to buy the spectral metric back was measured and
REJECTED before this re-fit and stays rejected. 0.001 would reach 56.5 dB, but 120 s
renders with the pedal held show the loop already creeping up at 0.0007 (last-5 s peak
1.70 -> 2.42) and diverging at 0.0014 (91.5 and climbing), so 0.001 sits in the
marginal-stability band. Do not retry it from the 56.5 dB figure alone. The re-fit above
leaves resonance_gain at 0.00025 and did not touch it.
----- earlier re-baseline, describing the 2026-08-22 pre-re-fit state -----
RE-BASELINE 2026-08-22, noteResonator unity-peak normalisation (`piano/resonance.go`).
The sympathetic-resonance path fed every undamped string through a bank of three two-pole
resonators built with b0 = 1-r, which is not unity-peak-normalised: each peaked at roughly
1/(2*sin(w0)), so the bank amplified by 183x at A0, 20x at C4 and 2.6x at C7. That 1/f0
error put the DWG core's summed resonance loop over unity with the sustain pedal held, and
a 40 s render grew from a peak of 3.2 at 1 s to 1.2e7. Normalising the resonators to unity
peak gain removes the error and the render decays instead (0.44 at 40 s).
That preset - like every preset in the repo - pins resonance_gain 0.00025, so it was
fitted, and this gate calibrated, against a renderer whose sympathetic path carried that
error. Removing it legitimately changed the spectrum. The level loss is register-dependent,
heaviest exactly where the runaway was: -45.3 dB at A0, -38.0 at MIDI 36, -26.1 at C4,
-14.2 at MIDI 84, -8.3 at MIDI 96.
What moved then:
score               0.5330 -> 0.5249  IMPROVED, threshold unchanged 0.57
time_rmse           0.1022 -> 0.1019  improved, threshold unchanged 0.112
envelope_rmse_db   10.801  -> 10.156  improved, threshold unchanged 11.75
decay_diff_db_per_s 5.428  ->  4.800  improved, threshold unchanged 5.9
spectral_rmse_db   52.89   -> 62.287  WORSE,    threshold LOOSENED  57.5 -> 67.0
score improved while spectral_rmse_db worsened because the two are not measuring the same
thing here. Under the frozen legacy-v1 norms the spectral component is saturated (see the
SPECTRAL CAVEAT above), so clamp01 pins its contribution at a constant 1.0 x 0.30 either
way and the raw dB move never reaches `score`. The raw value is still a real regression
signal, which is why it is gated separately - and why the fence had to move rather than be
ignored. That widened fence has now been closed by the re-fit above.
----- earlier re-baseline, describing the 2026-08-21 state -----
Re-baselined on 2026-08-21 after the DWG string core stopped emitting a DC offset.
Before that change the C4 render carried DC as a first-order component, not as a
rounding error. Two measurement points, because they give different ratios and only
one of them is what analysis.Compare scores:
raw string-bank output, before output_gain and the body IR, second second of a held
note 60: mean +0.606 against an AC RMS of 0.376, a DC/AC ratio of 1.61.
rendered candidate at this gate's own render settings (the block above), which is
the signal Compare actually sees: mean +0.0325 against an AC RMS of 0.0652, a ratio
of 0.50, or 44.6% of total RMS. The reference reference/c4.wav is DC-free for
comparison: mean +0.000145 against an RMS of 0.0952, 0.15%.
The body IR and the output gain attenuate the offset but do not remove it, which is
why the ratio drops from 1.61 to 0.50 between the two points.
Removing it moved the metrics in both directions, and all four moves are consistent
with the DC having been counted as signal:
time_rmse           0.1104 -> 0.1022  improved, threshold TIGHTENED 0.12  -> 0.112
spectral_rmse_db    58.18  -> 52.89   improved, threshold TIGHTENED 63.5  -> 57.5
envelope_rmse_db     9.008 -> 10.801  worse,    threshold LOOSENED  9.8   -> 11.75
decay_diff_db_per_s  3.177 ->  5.428  worse,    threshold LOOSENED  3.45  ->  5.9
score                0.5194 -> 0.5330 worse by 2.6%, still inside the unchanged 0.57
The envelope and decay terms got worse because the DC was propping the envelope up:
the candidate decay slope goes from -8.9 to -11.2 dB/s against the reference -5.8,
so the model then decayed too fast where before a non-decaying offset hid it. Both of
those loosened fences are now tighter than they were before that re-baseline.
Scores recorded before 2026-08 are NOT comparable: analysis/distance.go changed six
times between 2026-02-14 and 2026-08-16 (phase detection, normalisation), so the
0.3839 in assets/presets/fitted-c4-mayfly.json.report.json was produced by a
different metric implementation.
